title: The Naughty Boy

full_text:
Once upon a time, an old poet sat by his cozy hearth on a stormy evening. Outside, rain beat furiously against the windowpanes, and the wind howled through the chimney like a wounded beast.

"How fortunate I am to sit here in the warm shelter of my study," said the old poet to himself, stirring the glowing embers.

Suddenly, a faint knock sounded at the door, accompanied by a child's plaintive cry: "Open the door, kind sir! I am shivering with cold, and the rain has soaked through all my clothes!"

The tender-hearted poet hastened to unbolt the door. There stood a little boy, completely naked, shivering from head to foot. Rain dripped from his golden curls, his lips were blue with frost, and behind his shoulders hung a pair of delicate, sodden wings. In his small hands, he held a tiny wooden bow and a quiver of painted arrows.

"Poor little creature!" said the poet with fatherly compassion. He carried the child to the fireside, warmed his freezing hands in his own, wrapped him in a warm dry woolen blanket, and fed him sweet wine and roasted apples.

The boy soon revived. The rosy color returned to his cheeks, his eyes sparkled with mischievous merriment, and he began to jump about the rug in high spirits.

"What is your name, my cheerful little guest?" asked the old poet with a warm smile.

"My name is Cupid!" laughed the boy. "Do you not know me? Look, here is my bow! Oh, but alas, the rain has surely ruined my bowstring!"

The boy took up his bow, examined the taut hemp, placed a sharp little arrow upon the notch, drew the string back to his ear, and aimed straight at the old poet's chest. Twang! The arrow pierced the poet right through the heart!

"Ha, ha, ha!" laughed the naughty boy, clapping his hands and dancing with glee. "My bowstring was not spoiled after all!" And with that, he spread his golden wings and flew straight out through the window into the stormy night.

The old poet lay clutching his wounded chest, for the arrow was tipped with love's burning fire. "Fie upon that treacherous boy!" he groaned. He warned all his young friends never to open their doors to the cunning little archer, but Cupid wanders the world in disguise to this very day, shooting his mischievous darts into unsuspecting hearts.
moral: Beware the unpredictable arrows of sudden infatuation, for passion often hides behind the guise of helplessness.
